A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Point-SAM and its SAM-assisted data engine. The complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables and equations, are readable and support reliable comparison despite restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original point-prompted segmentation, object-proposal, few-shot segmentation and ablation results in Section 5, plus an AGILE3D normalization experiment in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds tokenizer comparisons, efficiency measurements, training controls and additional quantitative and qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 introduces a Voronoi tokenizer as an alternative to v1's KNN-based patch tokenization. Points are assigned to their nearest sampled center, processed with an MLP and aggregated using scatter-max. This changes both point-cloud and mask-prompt encoding; the main decoder, losses and pseudo-label pipeline remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The training mixture and principal task families remain unchanged. v2 extends evaluation with Waymo qualitative cases, additional Polycam/Objaverse demonstrations, StorageFurniture interior segmentation and point-prompted segmentation on Replica. Replica object proposals and ShapeNetPart few-shot segmentation already appeared in v1 and are retained in Appendix B.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain AGILE3D, MV-SAM, InterObject3D++, OpenMask3D, PointBERT and Uni3D. v2 adds an explicit pseudo-label-generation baseline using Point-SAM without 2D SAM in Table 5b, providing a new comparator for the data engine.

E3.justification: v2 replaces the main Large/Giant comparison with a controlled KNN/Voronoi comparison and introduces throughput/memory evaluation at different prompt counts, ScanNet-only training controls and alternative pseudo-label training conditions. Appendix H adds cropped-Replica interactive evaluation. Existing training schedules and standard IoU@k procedures are retained; the interior experiment's training mixture is inconsistently specified between Table 11 and Appendix G.

E4.justification: New analyses test tokenizer accuracy and efficiency, performance with training data matched to AGILE3D, and the contribution of SAM beyond self-generated pseudo labels. Table 10 extends training-mixture ablations beyond PartNet-Mobility to three other benchmarks, while Appendix G directly examines interior segmentation. The earlier patch-size and AGILE3D normalization studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. New result tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v1's Large scores reappear as KNN in v2 Table 3, while Giant rows disappear and Voronoi results are added. The new variant has mixed accuracy differences, including S3DIS IoU@10 of 87.3 versus KNN's 90.4. New efficiency results report KITTI360 throughput of 13.7 versus 5.2 shapes/second at ten prompts, and Tables 5 and 10–12 add further outcomes. Original proposal and few-shot scores remain unchanged in Table 7.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal assumptions, theorems or proofs. The retained mask-output equation is unchanged apart from notation; the Voronoi addition describes an algorithmic component without introducing a separate theoretical derivation.

C1.justification: v2 makes the novel, efficient Voronoi tokenizer a headline contribution, adding a substantive efficiency claim to the original segmentation and distillation contributions. The introduction also replaces the explicit model-and-dataset scaling contribution with an emphasis on demonstrated transferability and foundation-model positioning.

C2.justification: v2 adds hypotheses about AGILE3D's ScanNet-specific design overfitting, interpretations of self-generated versus SAM-assisted pseudo labels, and dataset-dependent transfer effects in Appendix E. It also explains the tokenizer's efficiency benefit. The concluding limitations concerning data scale, computation and dependence on SAM labels are retained.

D1.justification: v2 specifies RTX-4090 hardware for the timing experiment and procedural details for new controls and qualitative probing. It removes the explicit pretrained-Uni3D model-size description and the CUDA prompt-sampling implementation disclosure. Appendix A's optimizer, schedules, hardware and augmentation recipe, and the code/demo link, remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds citations including SANeRF-HQ and SERF while retaining its existing positioning against lifted 2D segmentation, 3D foundation models and interactive methods. The widespread conversion from numbered to author-year citations is stylistic rather than an expansion of research coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and encoder explanation receive focused rewrites, alongside affiliation and terminology edits. Original Sections 5.2–5.3 move to Appendices B.1–B.2, and ablations become Section 5.2. Most existing prose and the top-level narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redesigned, with Figure 2 adding architecture, tokenizer and grouping panels. Figure 4 is restyled and gains prompt-color explanations. v2 adds Figures 5–7 and several new tables, relocates existing displays, and changes the document's title, heading and page styling.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the tokenizer measurements and new training/data-engine controls provide useful evidence about efficiency and the sources of performance gains. However, reporting problems limit the benefit: Table 5a gives KITTI360 IoU@5 as 87.1 where Table 3 gives 81.7, Table 9 labels 3.31-to-3.52 FPS as a 34.4% increase, and the interior experiment has conflicting training descriptions. The revision strengthens empirical support overall, but these reliability and reproducibility defects prevent a major improvement.
